t: Section 3320(b)(4)(A)(i) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking “more than the standard 128 semester (or 192 quarter) credit hours” and inserting “at least the standard 120 semester (or 180 quarter) credit hours”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to title 38 that changes a credit-hour threshold from more than 128 semester hours to at least 120 semester hours. No tempting contrary reading exists: it involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute regarding the number of credit hours required for veterans' education benefits. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in a federal decision-making process. It simply changes a numerical threshold for eligibility.
qwen_block.s: Section 3320(b)(4)(A)(i) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking “more than the standard 128 semester (or 192 quarter) credit hours” and inserting “at least the standard 120 semester (or 180 quarter) credit hours”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that replaces the credit-hour threshold in 38 U.S.C. 3320(b)(4)(A)(i) ("more than the standard 128 semester" becomes "at least the standard 120 semester"). No outside party is consulted, heard, given a comment period, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is authorized. The link to education benefits is not participation, because benefit eligibility and applications are expressly excluded.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Section 3320 of title 38 deals with veterans' education benefits. Someone might read the reference to credit-hour thresholds as touching on applications for benefits, but under the definition, applying for benefits is not participation anyway. More importantly, this section only changes a numeric eligibility threshold. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue. It also doesn't authorize any rulemaking.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statutory eligibility requirement for educational benefits by changing a credit hour threshold. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties (such as students, schools, or the public) to consult with, comment to, or participate in the federal government's decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this text relates to the criteria for such benefits rather than a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 3320(b)(4)(A)(i) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking “more than the standard 128 semester (or 192 quarter) credit hours” and inserting “at least the standard 120 semester (or 180 quarter) credit hours”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing credit hour requirements affects student participation in benefits, but the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants. This section merely amends a numerical threshold for eligibility; it does not create a process for outside parties to consult with the government, comment on rules, or participate in decision-making.
